title: Naturality of the canonical presheaf-to-sheaf tensor map
statement: Let (C,J) be a site and R a sheaf of commutative rings. Let A,Aprime,B,Bprime be sheaves of R-modules, f:Aprime -> A and g:Bprime -> B. Write s(A,B) for homTensorSectionMap [lem-sc-hom-tensor-degreewise], the unit of module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] followed by the underlying inverse of the sheaf tensor comparison [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then s(Aprime,Bprime);(f tensor g).val = (f.val tensor g.val);s(A,B), an equality of presheaf module morphisms. No invertibility of f or g, boundedness, or hypothesis on sections is imposed.

source.place: Section 03EK (tensor product as sheafification), and Lemma 03CY (module sheafification universal property); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03EK and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03CY

proof.text: Apply homTensorComparison_natural [lem-sc-hom-tensor-comparison-natural] to f,g. Compose with the inverse comparison on both sides using Iso.inv_comp_eq and the inverse identities. Apply SheafOfModules.Hom.val to obtain the equality of underlying presheaf morphisms.

Precompose with the sheafification unit at Aprime.val tensor Bprime.val. Its naturality moves f.val tensor g.val across the unit. Unfold homTensorSectionMap and reassociate. This proves the displayed identity for arbitrary maps, including identity and zero maps, without sectionwise surjectivity.

proof_origin.place: Section 03EK and Lemma 03CY; existing two-step plan made into Lean, with the first step isolated in homTensorComparison_natural.

Mathlib provides tensorHom_app and tensorator naturality. The source MonoidalClosed has comparison naturality only with identical site and coefficient universes. SheafificationTensor.tensorPure_natural is private and has the same universe restriction. No public general-site theorem matches this signature. lean.statement: theorem homTensorSectionMap_natural {A A' B B' : Mod} (f : A' ⟶ A) (g : B' ⟶ B) : letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory R homTensorSectionMap R A' B' ≫ (f ⊗ₘ g).val = (f.val ⊗ₘ g.val) ≫ homTensorSectionMap R A B
